week_in_brief: Coverage contractions and care delivery disruption arrived in the same week, narrowing the margin for healthcare marketing teams still operating on last year's assumptions.

items.headline: MEDICAID CUTS AREN'T A POLICY STORY — THEY'RE A PATIENT ACQUISITION STORY
items.whats_happening: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act is projected to cut federal Medicaid spending by $911 billion over 10 years, with RAND Health projecting state budgets will fall $664 billion between 2025 and 2035. ACA enrollment losses tied to the same legislation are already reshaping how insurers model 2026. For regional health systems, this is a payer mix event — the ratio of covered versus self-pay patients in your service area will shift, and service line demand will follow. Rural and safety-net hospitals face the highest closure risk, but virtually every regional system will see patient population composition change.
items.so_what: Audit your service line messaging now for coverage assumptions that are no longer accurate. Financial assistance program content — eligibility, enrollment support, alternative care pathways — needs to move from the bottom of your site to the front of your acquisition strategy before patients disenroll and disappear.

items.headline: HOSPITAL-AT-HOME IS GROWING. YOUR AD TARGETING ISN'T.
items.whats_happening: Advocate Health is scaling its hospital-at-home program, delivering acute care in patients' residences and decoupling care access from physical facility location. At the same time, Meta is on track to fully automate advertising by end of 2026 — targeting, creative, copy, and optimization driven by AI with minimal human control. These two trends are on a collision course. Ad automation systems are built around facility geography and physical catchment areas. As home-based care extends your service area beyond drive-time radius, automated targeting will default to assumptions your care model has already outgrown.
items.so_what: Map your home-based care eligibility zones before platform automation locks in your geographic parameters for you. If Advantage+ or Performance Max campaigns are already running, audit where impressions are actually being served versus where your eligible patient population actually lives.

items.headline: CMS JUST CREATED A NEW CATEGORY TO MARKET — WITH GUARDRAILS BUILT IN
items.whats_happening: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS — the federal agency overseeing Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement) has established a formal reimbursement category for digital mental health treatments (DMHTs): FDA-cleared software-based therapeutics now billable as a medical device class. Nine products are approved so far, including SleepioRx for insomnia and DaylightRx for anxiety. For health systems with behavioral health service lines, this creates a real marketing opportunity: digital mental health products can now be positioned alongside traditional care with a legitimate reimbursement pathway. The complication is that a separate industry analysis this week identified evolving patient expectations, shifting regulatory requirements (including HIPAA enforcement and privacy scrutiny), and AI personalization tools as converging forces that are making healthcare marketing significantly more complex. A new clinical-adjacent category like DMHTs sits at the intersection of all three.
items.so_what: If you have a behavioral health line, start by inventorying which FDA-cleared digital therapeutics your system offers or partners with — then confirm your consent management and data governance infrastructure before building campaigns around them. The opportunity is real; the compliance exposure is equally real.

items.headline: YOUR MEASUREMENT TOOLS ARE GETTING BETTER. YOUR DATA HAS TO CATCH UP.
items.whats_happening: Google launched Meridian Studio — an enterprise media mix modeling (MMM) platform — and updated GeoX, its tool for measuring actual marketing lift by geographic region. The promise: multi-location health systems can now test whether campaigns in specific markets are actually driving patient volume, not just generating impressions. Meanwhile, the State of Martech 2026 report found the marketing technology landscape has essentially plateaued at 15,505 products, with AI now surfacing the integration gaps and data quality problems that vendor growth was masking. And Infosys's acquisition of Optimum Healthcare IT signals accelerating consolidation of the healthcare IT and digital transformation vendor market — meaning platform roadmaps are becoming less predictable.
items.so_what: Sophisticated measurement tools are available, but they only work with clean, connected data. Health systems with fragmented CRM infrastructure, incomplete patient journey tracking, or disconnected EHR-to-marketing pipelines will not be able to take advantage of them. This is the year to prioritize data hygiene — not as a future investment, but as the prerequisite for every measurement capability now on the table.

this_weeks_take: Healthcare marketers are being asked to do more — clearer messaging for patients losing coverage, expanded geographic targeting for patients receiving care at home, governance infrastructure for emerging clinical-adjacent products — while every external cost and complexity signal is moving in the wrong direction. The teams that will hold their footing aren't the ones with the biggest budgets. They're the ones who've built the infrastructure to know what's actually working.
